drivingQuestion: How can Rava treat the fallen ox as Pit according to Rav?
outcomeNote: Rava's statement re-transmitted in a form that avoids the difficulty

segments.he: הָנִיחָא לִשְׁמוּאֵל, דְּאָמַר: כֹּל תַּקָּלָה – בּוֹר הוּא. אֶלָּא לְרַב, דְּאָמַר: עַד דְּמַפְקַר לֵיהּ, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר?
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «This works out well according to» the opinion of «Shmuel, who says: Any obstruction is» categorized as «Pit,» and the same halakha exempting the one responsible for the pit from damage to utensils applies to them as well. «But according to» the opinion of «Rav, who says» that one’s property is not categorized as Pit «until he renounces ownership of it, what is there to say?» Presumably, the owner did not renounce ownership of the ox or even of the carcass.

segments.he: אֶלָּא אִי אִיתְּמַר – הָכִי אִיתְּמַר, אָמַר רָבָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁהִבְאִישׁ מִגּוּפוֹ, אֲבָל הִבְאִישׁ מֵרֵיחוֹ – פָּטוּר. מַאי טַעְמָא? גְּרָמָא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא, וּגְרָמָא בְּעָלְמָא לָא מִיחַיַּיב.
segments.en: «Rather, if» this statement «was stated, it was stated like this: Rava says» that «they taught» this halakha «only» in the case «where» the ox «contaminated» the water «with its body,» i.e., its carcass. «But» if it «contaminated» the water «with its stench,» the owner is «exempt. What is the reason?» It is because the damage «is» caused «merely» by «an indirect» action. Although the ox’s owner was initially responsible for his animal falling into the pit, the stench did not result directly from this action. It subsequently occurred on its own, «and» one is «not liable» for damage that is caused «merely» by «an indirect» action.

moves.summary: Rava's Pit reasoning fails for Rav, who requires renunciation

moves.cueHe: אלא אי איתמר הכי איתמר אמר רבא
moves.summary: revised version: liable only if contaminated by its body, not its stench
